html:
Nanyue was a kingdom in today's southern China and northern Vietnam, ruled from Panyu, now Guangzhou, from 204 to 111 BCE.

Its founder, Zhao Tuo, was a general of the Qin dynasty sent to conquer the Yue peoples of the south. When the Qin fell, he cut the mountain roads to the north and made himself king. He took up local Yue customs and ruled Chinese settlers and Yue alike. He later conquered the kingdom of Au Lac in the Red River delta. He bowed to the Han emperors in name, yet for a time called himself emperor at home.

Five kings ruled Nanyue. In 112 BCE a dispute at court gave Emperor Wu of Han his chance, and the Han conquered Nanyue in 111 BCE. The rich tomb of its second king was found in Guangzhou in 1983. In Vietnamese history, Nanyue is remembered as Nam Viet, an early state of Vietnam's north. See also its neighbour Minyue.
sum: Nanyue was a kingdom in today's southern China and northern Vietnam, ruled from Panyu, now Guangzhou, from 204 to 111 BCE.
